title: Hannah
lead: The mother of Samuel. Childless and taunted, she prayed silently at Shiloh, vowed her son to the LORD, and then sang the song of reversal (1 Samuel 2:1–10) that lies behind Mary's song in Luke 1.

sections.b: Hannah is one of the Bible's barren women whose sons come as God's gift (see the topic on barrenness). Her story is short, 1 Samuel 1:1–2:21, but it shapes the whole book: her prayer opens it, and her song, with its closing line about the LORD's king and "his anointed" (1 Samuel 2:10), announces kingship before Israel has a king. The song's themes, the proud brought low and the poor lifted up, return in David's song at the end of the books of Samuel (2 Samuel 22) and in the songs of Mary and Zechariah in Luke 1. The rabbis drew rules for prayer from her (Bavli Berakhot 31a), and her story is read in synagogues on Rosh Hashanah.
